To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
human T‐cell lymphocytes can be cytotoxic in vitro against cultivated human tumor cells of the histological type of the tumor of the respective lymphocytes.
human peripheral blood T‐cells, separated from the T‐cell rich fraction, are cytotoxic against tumor cells in vitro.

Tumor‐specific cytotoxicity is mediated by human peripheral blood lymphocytes (PBL) which can be separated into two fractions by the ability of these cells to form spontaneous rosettes with erythrocytes of sheep (E).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cytotoxic activity of human peripheral blood lymphocytes on human tumor cell lines.
the cytotoxic activity of human T‐cells on cultivated cells of human tumors.
the cytotoxic activity of human T‐lymphocytes on cultivated tumor cells, with the aim of studying this activity in patients with malignant disease.

human T‐lymphocytes, in the absence of other cells, are capable of cytotoxicity in vitro against cells of a malignant tumor of the same histologic type as the tumor of the lymphocyte donor.

the cytotoxicity of human T‐cells against tumor cells is a phenomenon which is not only restricted to the allogeneic system but can be observed also in the autologous system.
